rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns (bot spam + 'thanks'), so recall is vacuous for both. Both candidates independently find the same core defect (unmarked test file silently deselected by CI's marker-based selection) and both catch that warmup_quack_fp8() bypasses the new gate — but X correctly rates the warmup bypass as a hard blocker (it can raise an uncaught OpError on the exact GPUs the PR claims to protect) while Y buries it as a 'nit', a real severity miscalibration. X also adds two higher-value, well-reasoned findings absent from Y (a sticky-disable/circuit-breaker design fix for the per-GEMM retry amplifier, and a plausible warning_once dedup-by-exception-object defect), each with concrete code diffs. Y's extra volume is mostly lower-value padding (asking to mark PR-body benchmark numbers as 'vendor-provided', a missing sm_101 test permutation) and some redundancy (sm_110a exclusion raised twice), diluting its signal-to-noise versus X's tighter, more decisively actionable review.
